author: harness:claude-code
message: List consolidation realizes the one-screen discovery story

author: harness:claude-code
message: Sequencing evidence 2026-07-31: 18 output-bounding flag spellings across 19 read commands, widest pairwise availability disagreement 10, four read surfaces with zero bounding flags; two recorded simplification axes conclude noun consolidation is a null move until the bounding set is uniform

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Payoff measured 2026-08-14, at HEAD build 2026.8.14. This task previously carried a rationale and no number; it now has one, and the number is large enough to reorder it.

The eight list variants render these help payloads:

    list-all             6,792 bytes
    list                 6,791
    list-blocked         6,687
    list-in-progress     6,642
    list-draft           6,639
    list-closed          6,627
    list-open            6,622
    list-canceled        6,616

Total 53,416 bytes, which is 25.2 percent of the 212,233-byte top-level help surface across all 71 canonical commands.

They are not merely similar. Measured line by line, each variant is 95 to 96 percent identical to plain list: 107 of 111 lines for list-open, list-closed, list-draft, list-in-progress and list-canceled; 109 of 113 for list-all; 107 of 112 for list-blocked. Ninety-eight lines totalling 6,188 bytes are byte-identical across all eight simultaneously.

Keeping one copy of those 98 shared lines recovers 43,316 bytes. That is 81.1 percent of this family's payload and 20.4 percent of the entire agent-facing help surface, from one consolidation.

For comparison, the whole surface shrank by 1,531 bytes at the root between 2026-08-13 and 2026-08-14 while per-command help grew by 48,848. This single task is roughly 28 times the size of the largest consolidation delivered so far, and it recovers slightly less than the surface grew in one day.

Two consequences for sequencing.

First, the payoff does not depend on the grammar decision. The 43,316 bytes are duplicated text, and deduplicating help content is available whether or not the eight spellings ever merge into pm list --status. The alias-preserving consolidation this task describes remains the right end state; the text deduplication is the part that can land first and independently.

Second, the count is the wrong instrument for this epic and this family proves it. Retiring seven spellings moves the command count from 71 to 64, about 10 percent. It moves the surface an agent must read by 20.4 percent, and it does so almost entirely by removing text that said the same thing eight times.

Method note: measure with `while IFS= read -r` over pm contracts command_summaries[].command. Sixty of the 131 declared rows are multi-word subcommand paths, and an unquoted `for` loop word-splits them into separate invocations that fall through to root help, which inflates the total roughly sevenfold.
